column10: < eṣá-1 (2530). uī́ ṽ (4m) v.t. ‘to let go; to leave (behind); 1 to place’. Note change of length of root vowel in the paradigm. Pres. tṛ sùh uiɑ̄̀th ‘he places (s.th.)’. Pres. caus. 1 sùh uiɑ̄́th ‘he lets (s.o.) place (s.th.)’. Pres. caus. 2 sùh uthiɑ̄́th ‘he causes (s.o.) to have (a third person) place (s.th.)’. This is a homonym with the pres. caus. of uithʌ́ṽ. Pres. pasṣ sùh uizɑ̄̀th ‘he is placed’. Fuṭ tṛ sùh úīṣʌth ‘he will place (s.th.)’. Perf. tṛ sʌ́ỹ úī-ċhē ‘he has placed (s.th.). Aoṛ tṛ sʌ́ỹ úī or úīl ‘he placed (s.th.)’. Conṭ tṛ sùh ùiā̃ bḗth ‘he places (s.th.) continuously’. Conṭ pasṣ sùh uiā̃̀ bḗth ‘he is continuously placed’. Parṭ pres. tṛ úī̃- ‘while placing (s.th.)’. Parṭ pres. pasṣ uizʌ́ỹ- ‘while being placed’. Conv. tṛ úī-. Conḍ pres. tṛ uilū́ (-khʌ̀ỹ) ‘if (he) places (s.th.)’. Parṭ perf. tṛ m. uyḗl- (khʌ̀ỹ) ‘(he has) placed (s.th.)’ or ‘had (he) placed (s.th.)’, parṭ perf. f. uī́li- ‘(she has) placed (s.th.)’ or ‘had (she) placed (s.th.)’. Imp. sg. tṛ úī. Imp. pl. tṛ

Acc̣ to Berger < *choṭṭa- and kumārī́. However, this is a triple synonym compound: ﬁrst syllable cf. Kal. čhu ‘daughter’ (ﬁrst syllable < duhitŕ.- [6481], second syllable < *maṭṭa- [9723], and third syllable < kuḍa-1 [3245]); the different vowels in čhumuṭkēr are the result of (not uncommon) vowel leftshift and metaphony: at an intermediate stage *čhumaṭukuṛi the second -u- (a dimin. sufﬁx) shifted to the left, producing *čhumuṭkaṛi, and metaphony caused the present form of the ﬁnal vowel (cf. the different etymological interpretation of Bashir 2001: 11f.). column10: < *vīdhradhanus- (12052) despite Fussman’s astonishment over Turner’s reconstruction, “le sens proposé par T. pour ce composé (‘arc dans le ciel bleu’) me paraˆit assez curieux; le propre des arcs en ciel est d’apparaˆitre par le temps de pluie” (Atlas 13). The important point is not that the emergence of a rainbow indeed does require meteorologic conditions where parts of the sky have to be clear, but that the modern form of this word has to be understood as a karmadhāraya- compound and not as a tatpuruṣa- as both authors seem to take for granteḍ The modern representative of vīdhrá- can also mean ‘blue’ in Phal. Thus biẓō̃́ṛ originally meant ‘blue/green bow’. With this meaning it parallels exactly Pshṭ šna kāsa ‘rainbow’ which liṭ means ‘blue/green bow’. Moreover, this semantic pattern for ‘rainbow’ is not uncommon in the area, as there is also Pshṭ sra kāsa, liṭ ‘red bow’, and Woṭ. latúr kasōṭ, also meaning liṭ ‘red bow’.
